A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inceptive Transformer work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices A–C to v2 Appendices D–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across five tasks, including benchmark scores, cross-validation, ablations, statistical tests, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated backbones, convolution ablations, attention analyses, and a stacked-module experiment.

M1.justification: The main transformer–inception–attention–pooling–classifier architecture and training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix G introduces an implemented variant with two sequential inception modules; it is a limited architectural extension rather than a replacement for the original model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English emotion recognition and irony detection from TweetEval, Bengali emotion recognition, OHSUMED, and CAVES. The dataset statistics are unchanged, moving from v1 Table 1 to v2 Appendix B, Table 7.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2–3 add ModernBERT and DeBERTa v3 comparisons across all four English tasks. BioBERT-Large also becomes a comparator on CAVES, whereas v1 evaluated it only on OHSUMED. The earlier comparator rows are retained.

E3.justification: Existing sequence lengths, training budgets, optimization settings, metrics, and cross-validation construction remain unchanged. New experiments introduce single-kernel and convolution-free controls, one-versus-two-module configurations, and inceptive BioBERT-Large configurations.

E4.justification: v1 ablates only attention and the dense block. v2 Table 6 additionally tests each of four convolution kernels separately and removes convolution entirely, directly examining the central multi-scale contribution. Appendix G tests stacking depth; additional attention comparisons and an illustrative irony case broaden the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten runs per model and dataset, cross-validation means and standard deviations, distributions across runs, and Wilcoxon signed-rank testing at the 0.05 threshold. The added significance-test rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained main benchmark rows keep their scores, while v2 adds substantial results for new comparators and architectural controls. For example, Table 3 reports OHSUMED F1 scores of 56.71 for ModernBERT and 64.07 for iMB-128. The full-model OHSUMED ablation value changes from 73.32 to 72.34, matching the retained main result. Appendix G newly reports stacked-model scores of 71.97 on OHSUMED and 83.38 on irony.

T1.justification: The convolution, feature concatenation, attention, pooling, and classification equations are substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added architectural explanations introduce no new formal results.

C1.justification: The central contribution and reported 1%–14% improvement claim remain. v2 adds an abstract claim that multi-scale convolution outperforms individual kernels, explicitly claims integration into pretrained encoders without costly retraining or model-specific adjustments, and introduces a below-10% inference-overhead claim.

C2.justification: The original local-feature and attention-redistribution interpretation remains. v2 adds explanations for differing emotion/irony gains, a channel-selection heuristic, a redundancy or oversmoothing hypothesis for stacking, and an explicit limitation that performance on tasks dominated by long-range dependencies has not been tested.

D1.justification: New Appendix A specifies the baseline's final-layer CLS representation, dropout probability of 0.3, and linear classification head. Figure 4 newly identifies the layers supplying baseline and inceptive attention maps. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changes to the existing implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Multi-CLS BERT, DeBERTa v3, and ModernBERT, plus an encoder-versus-LLM discussion supported by three additional studies. It also makes its novelty claim explicit. The earlier positioning as a general architectural enhancement complementary to pretraining modifications remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, comparative-results narrative, and performance interpretation are extensively rewritten. Related work and limitations gain topical subheadings, model notation receives a dedicated explanation, and the appendices are reorganized around new baseline and dataset material while retaining the earlier supplements.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory overview figure, class-distribution charts, word clouds, and a stacking comparison. Performance and ablation tables expand substantially. Attention plots combine baseline and inceptive curves, introduce logarithmic axes in several panels, and add model comparisons; other plots are restyled and the dataset-statistics table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important gap in v1 by directly comparing the central multi-scale module with single-kernel and convolution-free alternatives. Together with additional backbone comparisons and the stacking experiment, this substantially strengthens empirical validation. Baseline implementation disclosure and the new long-range limitation also improve clarity. Some new reporting claims overreach: the below-10% overhead statement conflicts with Table 3's RoBERTa OHSUMED timings, which imply approximately 10.41%. This limited reporting problem does not outweigh the stronger supporting evidence.
